findings.confusion: The page doesn't say that FastAPI has to be installed first, or that this needs a uv project. In an empty folder Alex gets a command-not-found or 'no such command' error and doesn't know what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Link to the install/setup page at the top, or add a one-line `uv add "fastapi[standard]"` prerequisite.

findings.confusion: The code returns 'Hello World', but the page says the browser will show 'Hello FastAPI'. Alex may think the code was copied wrong or that something is broken.
findings.suggestion: Make the shown response match the code: {"message": "Hello World"}.

findings.confusion: The sample openapi.json lists an '/items/' path, but this app only defines '/'. Alex may wonder whether they missed a step.
findings.suggestion: Show '/' in the sample output, or note that the output is illustrative.

findings.section: Step 4: define the path operation function
findings.quote: In this case, it is an async function. You could also define it as a normal function instead of async def
findings.confusion: Alex doesn't know async/await. The page says async and plain functions both work but not why, so Alex doesn't know which to use. The page does show that plain `def` works, so Alex can push on.
findings.suggestion: Add a one-line note: 'If you're unsure, use plain def; async is explained later,' with a link.

summary: Alex can finish this page. The first run is the weak spot: the page doesn't say to name the file main.py or to install FastAPI, and the 'Hello FastAPI' output doesn't match the code, so Alex has to guess or re-read. The path/operation/decorator explanations are clear and pitched at the right level.
